Subject: Redlines to MSA — liability and breach section

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are our latest redlines to the MSA (Aptum_MSA_Redlines_v3.pdf). Key asks: 1) remove Redwood's 1x fees aggregate cap for data security incidents and replace with a 3x fees cap specific to breaches; 2) carve out regulatory fines and third-party claims from any limitation of liability; 3) preserve consequential damages exclusion except for claims arising from data breaches.

We flagged a request for a separate security addendum to spell out incident response SLA and a financial sub-limit for breach-related damages — see p.7 of the redlines. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a breach sub-cap tied to a multiplier of fees (they proposed 3x) and whether you have a standard security addendum we can review?

Samantha Chen

Laura / Aditya — high-level legal guidance below. Long version attached as a Word draft (Draft-Security-Addendum.docx).

1) Aggregate cap approach — keep our standard aggregate cap (1x fees) in the MSA but add a narrowly tailored security sub-limit for verified data breaches. Example language: "For security incidents constituting an unauthorized access or disclosure of Customer Data, liability shall be capped at the lesser of (a) $3,000,000 or (b) three times the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the incident, provided such liability is subject to the exclusions below." This preserves a single cap philosophy while giving customers a breach-specific remedy.

2) Carve-outs — we should resist a broad carve-out for regulatory fines. Instead propose that regulatory fines remain excluded from the monetary cap only to the extent that applicable law requires the party to pay such fines. For third-party claims (e.g., class actions), limit Redwood's indemnity to IP and data third-party claims and expressly exclude indirect/immaterial third-party punitive damages.

3) Consequential damages — keep broad exclusion; add explicit exception for documented direct damages arising solely from a covered data breach. Avoid opening the door to consequential categories (loss of business, reputational harm).

4) Security addendum — propose a short addendum tying incident response milestones to an incident credit schedule (small service credits or fixed sub-limit offsets) rather than open-ended monetary exposure. The attached draft gives an incident classification matrix and a capped financial remedy schedule.

Suggested next step: send Aptum our marked MSA (redlines embedded) plus the Draft-Security-Addendum and offer a 30-minute legal sync. I think pushing a 2x fees cap may be acceptable commercially, but we should offer up to 3x only with cross-constraints (e.g., MFN for regulatory fines limited to law-required fines, tight definition of "security incident" and proof requirements).

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: RE: MSA redlines — breach liability sub-cap and security addendum

Laura — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed Rishi's suggestions with our GC. Key responses:
- Aptum can accept a single MSA aggregate cap if the breach sub-limit is explicit and set at 3x fees (their preference) OR if we accept language that regulatory fines and statutory penalties are not subject to the cap.
- They are open to the security addendum approach, but want it to include a limited liquidated damages schedule (not just service credits) tied to incident severity.
- Aptum will not accept language that narrows the definition of "security incident" beyond the standard unauthorized access/disclosure test. They want a relatively broad trigger so they can pursue remedies without extra proof burdens.

Next steps per Aptum: please send Redwood's marked MSA + Draft-Security-Addendum and indicate whether Redwood can increase the breach sub-cap to 3x fees or provide the alternative (regulatory fines carve-out). They would like to lock language this week and initiate DocuSign.

Samantha Chen
Head of Procurement, Aptum Systems
